name: Thin Ribs-Tubular Bones Dysmorphism Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Thin Ribs-Tubular Bones Dysmorphism Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of markedly thin ribs
Dysmorphic changes in tubular bones including shortening and cortical thinning
Characteristic facial dysmorphism including midface hypoplasia and micrognathia
Respiratory insufficiency due to thoracic cage abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major criteria (thin ribs and tubular bone dysmorphism) with supportive clinical and radiological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but is not definitive due to limited data

searchTerms: baby smaller than expected in womb

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abnormality of pelvic girdle bone morphology

imaging: Chest X-ray showing markedly thin ribs
Skeletal survey demonstrating tubular bone dysmorphism and cortical thinning
Thoracic CT scan revealing restrictive thoracic cage deformity
genetic: No definitive gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance pattern
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic facial dysmorphism

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of bone fragility with frequent fractures
Narrow thoracic cage with short ribs but presence of polydactyly
Characteristic radiographic findings distinct from thin ribs

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonatal period
Failure to thrive with feeding difficulties
references: Orphanet: Thin Ribs-Tubular Bones Dysmorphism Syndrome - ORPHA:1506
Spranger J, et al. Skeletal Dysplasias: An Atlas of Genetic Disorders of Skeletal Development. 2019.
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) database
